# Typed objects

## `pyropdf.typed`

Typed views of PDF objects, one per object type of the Arlington PDF Model.

The descriptors that `pyropdf-schema` generates from the Arlington PDF
Model give each key of an object type its types, the object types it links
to, whether it is required or inheritable, its default, and its possible
values. A view reads and writes a `pyropdf.Dictionary`,
`pyropdf.Stream`, or `pyropdf.Array` handle by those rules:

```python
import pyropdf
from pyropdf import typed

with pyropdf.open("input.pdf") as doc:
    catalog = typed.Catalog(doc.catalog)
    root = catalog.Pages              # a PageTreeNodeRoot view
    page = typed.PageObject(doc.pages[0].obj)
    rotate = page.Rotate              # inherited from the page tree, else 0
    page.Rotate = 90                  # checked against the declared types
```

Each object type is a subclass of `View` named after it; a name that
begins with `3D` begins with `ThreeD` instead. An attribute reads or
writes a key whose name is an identifier, and indexing reads or writes any
key or array element. Reading converts a value to its declared type:

- `integer` and `bitmask` read as `int`, `number` as `int` or
  `pyropdf.Real`, and `boolean` as `bool`;
- `name` reads as `pyropdf.Name`; `string-text`,
  `string-ascii`, and `date` as `str`; `string` and `string-byte`
  as `pyropdf.String`;
- `rectangle` reads as a tuple of four floats as stored, and `matrix` as
  a `pyropdf.Matrix`;
- a container that links to object types reads as the view of the linked
  type that its `/Type`-like keys match, a container that links to none
  as its handle, and `name-tree` and `number-tree` as their dictionary.

An inheritable key absent from its object is read from the nearest
`/Parent` that holds it, and a key absent everywhere reads as its default
when the model gives one. An absent optional key reads as `None` through an
attribute, and a `null` value counts as absent (ISO 32000-2 section 7.3.7).
A required key that is absent, and a value of no declared type, raise
`pyropdf.PdfError`. Predicates of the model are not evaluated here;
the structural check evaluates them. Use `view.interpret(key)` to apply the
model's type, link and value conditions to one entry of the current version.

Writing takes the Python form of a declared type, or a view or handle for a
container type, and refuses anything else with `TypeError`, or a name
outside the key's possible values with `ValueError`. Assigning `None` to
an attribute removes the key, unless the key may be `null`.

`typed.pyi`, which tools/arlington/generate.py writes, declares each view's
keys with their types for type checkers.

## `typed.ArrayView`

```python
class ArrayView(View)
```

The base of the views of array types.

### `obj`

```python
typed.ArrayView.obj: pyropdf.Dictionary | pyropdf.Array
```

The viewed handle.

### `create`

```python
typed.ArrayView.create(
    document: Document,
    values: Mapping[str, Any] | list[Any] | tuple[Any, ...] | pyropdf.Array,
    /,
    *,
    data: bytes | None = None,
    attach: Callable[[Self], None] | None = None,
) -> Self
```

Create an indirect object from PDF values and check its required references.

Supply dictionary keys, or an ordered sequence for an array, using
indirect handles for required references. Stream descriptors accept
decoded bytes as `data`. The new object and its validation form one
undo step, including inside an existing transaction. An optional
`attach(view)` callback can register the new object in its owner's
collection and build reciprocal links before validation.

### `replace`

```python
typed.ArrayView.replace(value: object, /)
```

Replace this indirect object's value, preserving its number and generation.

The replacement must satisfy this descriptor and every supported live
incoming link. Coupled or unknown relationships require their owning
operation. Accept PDF values, a container handle or a typed view.

### `remove`

```python
typed.ArrayView.remove()
```

Free this indirect object when it has no live incoming reference.

### `interpret`

```python
typed.ArrayView.interpret(key: str | int, /) -> Any
```

Interpret a declared entry in its document's current version.

Return the selected linked view, scalar, default, or `None` for an
absent optional value. A name or number tree returns a `LinkedTree`
whose `lookup` resolves and interprets an individual leaf. An ambiguous link, an unresolved reference,
or a value outside the admitted types and values raises PdfError.

### `__getitem__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__getitem__(key: str | int) -> Any
```

Return the typed value of `key`; raise `KeyError` when it is absent.

### `__getattr__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__getattr__(name: str) -> Any
```

Return the typed value of the key `name`, or `None` when it is absent.

### `__setitem__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__setitem__(key: str | int, value: object)
```

Write `value` under `key` as one of its declared types.

### `__setattr__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__setattr__(name: str, value: object)
```

Write the key `name`; `None` removes it unless it may be `null`.

### `__delitem__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__delitem__(key: str | int)
```

Remove `key`; raise `KeyError` when it is absent.

### `__delattr__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__delattr__(name: str)
```

Remove the key `name`.

### `__contains__`

```python
typed.ArrayView.__contains__(key: object) -> bool
```

Return whether `key` is stored in the object itself.

## `typed.LinkedTree`

```python
typed.LinkedTree(tree: pyropdf.Dictionary, descriptor: str, key: str)
```

A name or number tree with the Arlington types declared for its leaf values.

### `xref`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.xref: int | None
```

The object number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `generation`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.generation: int | None
```

The generation number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `is_indirect`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.is_indirect: bool
```

Whether this is an indirect object rather than a direct value inside one.

### `__len__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of entries or elements.

### `geospatial_measure`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.geospatial_measure: GeospatialMeasure | None
```

Read the registration of this viewport, image, form or Geospatial3D annotation.

Settable.

### `geospatial_point`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.geospatial_point(
    index: int,
    /,
) -> tuple[tuple[Decimal, ...], tuple[Decimal, ...]]
```

Return a registered owner-space point and its geographic or projected coordinates.

A viewport or form uses its PDF bounding box, an image uses the unit
square, and a Geospatial3D annotation uses its view world coordinates.
Geographic data returns latitude then longitude, projected data easting
then northing. A three-dimensional registration also returns elevation.

### `xmp`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.xmp: str | None
```

The UTF-8 XMP packet of this PDF resource, or `None` when absent.

For example, `page.obj.xmp` reads page metadata. The packet must
contain an XML RDF element and fit in 1 MiB. Invalid packets raise
`MalformedPdfError` and oversized packets raise `LimitError`
with code `stream_data_size`. Assign a packet or delete the property
to change this resource's association. Other owners keep their packet.

Settable.

### `__getitem__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__getitem__(key: str) -> Any
```

Return the resolved value of `key`.

### `__setitem__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__setitem__(key: str, value: object)
```

Write `value` under `key`.

### `__delitem__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__delitem__(key: str)
```

Remove `key`.

### `__iter__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__iter__() -> Iterator[str]
```

Iterate over the keys as `Name` values.

### `__contains__`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.__contains__(key: object) -> bool
```

Return whether `key` is present, without resolving its value.

### `lookup`

```python
typed.LinkedTree.lookup(key: bytes | int, /) -> Any
```

Return the typed value for a stored byte-string or integer key, raising KeyError if absent.
